variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: An AI agent is a software system that uses a model to decide what to do next, calls bounded tools to affect or inspect an environment, observes the result, and continues until it reaches a stopping condition.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Choose the smallest architecture that can finish the job”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Direct router
pairs.detail: Classify the request and call one known tool.
pairs.explanation: Classify the request and call one known tool. This is fast and inspectable for narrow tasks with a stable route.

pairs.label: Plan and execute
pairs.detail: Create a bounded plan, execute one step at a time, and re-plan only when an observation invalidates the next step.
pairs.explanation: Create a bounded plan, execute one step at a time, and re-plan only when an observation invalidates the next step.

pairs.label: Supervisor and workers
pairs.detail: A supervisor delegates typed subtasks to specialized workers.
pairs.explanation: A supervisor delegates typed subtasks to specialized workers. Parallelism helps only when dependencies and merge rules are explicit.

pairs.label: Long-running workflow
pairs.detail: Persist checkpoints around queues, approvals, and external events.
pairs.explanation: Persist checkpoints around queues, approvals, and external events. A durable workflow engine owns time and retries; the model does not.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. Agents matter when a task cannot be completed by one model response.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Direct router: Classify the request and call one known tool. variants.title: Give each part its job

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Memory is scoped state with a lifecycle”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Working state
pairs.detail: Keep the goal, current plan, typed observations, pending approvals, and remaining budget.
pairs.explanation: Keep the goal, current plan, typed observations, pending approvals, and remaining budget. Discard it when the run ends unless the product needs a durable trace.

pairs.label: Durable task state
pairs.detail: Persist checkpoints, side-effect IDs, owner, deadline, and status so a process restart does not repeat completed work.
pairs.explanation: Persist checkpoints, side-effect IDs, owner, deadline, and status so a process restart does not repeat completed work.

pairs.label: Retrieved knowledge
pairs.detail: Search approved sources with provenance, access checks, freshness, and relevance.
pairs.explanation: Search approved sources with provenance, access checks, freshness, and relevance. Retrieved instructions remain untrusted unless policy grants them authority.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Put deterministic control around probabilistic decisions”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Validate the proposal
pairs.detail: Parse a typed action, reject unknown tools and arguments, and preserve the evidence used to propose it.
pairs.explanation: Parse a typed action, reject unknown tools and arguments, and preserve the evidence used to propose it.

pairs.label: Authorize the effect
pairs.detail: Compare required scope with the task's delegated authority.
pairs.explanation: Compare required scope with the task's delegated authority. Request approval before high-impact or exceptional actions.

pairs.label: Execute once
pairs.detail: Use deadlines, isolation, rate limits, and idempotency keys so timeout and retry behavior cannot create hidden duplicate effects.
pairs.explanation: Use deadlines, isolation, rate limits, and idempotency keys so timeout and retry behavior cannot create hidden duplicate effects.

pairs.label: Verify and record
pairs.detail: Read back the authoritative state, append an audit event, and stop when success, denial, budget exhaustion, or a terminal failure is proven.
pairs.explanation: Read back the authoritative state, append an audit event, and stop when success, denial, budget exhaustion, or a terminal failure is proven.

variants.title: Make the decision
variants.context: An AI agent is a software system that uses a model to decide what to do next, calls bounded tools to affect or inspect an environment, observes the result, and continues until it reaches a stopping condition.
variants.prompt: What separates an AI agent from a single model response?
options: An agent always uses a larger model
An agent runs a bounded loop that chooses actions, observes results, and stops against an explicit goal
An agent stores every conversation forever
An agent can execute any tool without approval
variants.explanation: The defining systems behavior is the controlled feedback loop: decide, act through bounded tools, observe authoritative results, and stop under a task contract.

variants.title: Make the decision
variants.context: An AI agent is a software system that uses a model to decide what to do next, calls bounded tools to affect or inspect an environment, observes the result, and continues until it reaches a stopping condition.
variants.prompt: A refund request times out after the payment API may have accepted it. What should the agent do?
options: Retry immediately with a new request ID
Ask the model whether the first call probably worked
Read authoritative payment state using the same idempotency key before deciding whether to retry
Increase the agent's iteration limit
variants.explanation: Timeout does not prove failure. Read-after-write verification and a stable idempotency key prevent an uncertain response from becoming a duplicate side effect.

A long-running autonomous workflow

variants.prompt: Which information belongs in durable task state for a resumable agent?

Every document the agent has ever retrieved
Confirmed side-effect IDs, checkpoint status, owner, deadline, and pending approvals
A copy of the user's credentials
variants.explanation: Durable state must let the workflow resume without replaying completed effects. It should preserve typed checkpoints and control data, not unbounded context or secrets.

variants.prompt: What is the strongest evidence that an agent architecture is better than a fixed workflow?
options: Its execution traces contain more steps
It uses planning for every request
It improves task success on representative slices enough to justify its added latency, cost, and control risk
It can call the largest number of tools
variants.explanation: Autonomy is an engineering trade-off. It should earn its complexity through measured task outcomes while staying within reliability, safety, latency, and cost constraints.
